A worldwide pandemic of the disease COVID-19, caused by the virus SARS-CoV-2, which began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. It spread across the world in early 2020 and killed millions of people.

The World Health Organization declared a public health emergency on 30 January 2020 and called it a pandemic on 11 March. Wuhan was locked down in January, and in the following months most countries closed borders, schools and businesses. Hospitals in places like northern Italy and New York were overwhelmed. Where the virus came from, whether from animals at a Wuhan market or from a laboratory, is still disputed.

What it brought:

  • Officially counted deaths passed seven million; estimates of excess deaths are far higher.
  • Vaccines came in record time. The BioNTech and Pfizer mRNA vaccine was approved in December 2020, less than a year after the virus was sequenced.
  • Lockdowns caused the sharpest global recession since the 1930s, then supply chain shortages and inflation.
  • Remote work, online school and home delivery spread fast and partly stayed.

China kept a strict "zero Covid" policy of mass testing and lockdowns until December 2022, longer than anywhere else, then dropped it suddenly. The WHO ended the global emergency in May 2023.

It was the worst pandemic in a century, one in a long line on this chart from the Black Death to the SARS outbreak of 2002, which had also started in China.
sum: A worldwide pandemic of the disease COVID-19, caused by the virus SARS-CoV-2, which began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. It spread across the world in early 2020 and killed millions of people.
